title: And they teach the serpents there to entwine themselves up on long sticks out of the ground and of the scales of these serpents they brew out a brewage like to mead.
html_source:
This seems to refer to the brewing of beer. This is consistent with the foregoing sentences, and also with hopvine “serpents” that are trained to grow up sticks (see background of photo), producing their bitter “scales”.

I think this refers to the cultivation of grape vines, and then to the production of wine. The “serpents” are tendrils.
